items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.3, its most powerful model to date
items.summary_en: On September 2, 2026, Meta's AI Research team and its official 'AI at Meta' account announced the release of Muse Spark 1.3, describing improved performance on agentic and coding tasks and a focus on real-world usability. Meta said the model can sustain longer-horizon work across multiple workflows in a single thread, asks clarifying questions and flags when it is stuck, and is better calibrated about its own limits instead of producing unsupported answers. Meta also said the update uses roughly 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than the prior Muse Spark 1.2 version to complete comparable tasks.
items.notes: Corroborated by Meta's official 'AI at Meta' account on X (https://x.com/AIatMeta/status/2095234385129963666) and the developer.meta.com model page, both cited in secondary reporting (Axios, Bloomberg, SiliconANGLE, all dated Sept 2, 2026). Direct fetch of research.meta.ai, ai.meta.com, x.com and developer.meta.com was blocked by the network egress proxy this session; facts are drawn from WebSearch result snippets quoting the official posts, not a fully fetched page. Press-reported pricing ($1.25/$4.25 per million tokens standard tier) and a reported ranking (around #6 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index) could not be independently verified against the primary source in this session and are omitted from the summary pending confirmation.

coverage_note: Access limitation this run: WebFetch was blocked by the network egress proxy for every domain attempted (Meta-owned and third-party alike), so no page could be read directly; all findings rely on WebSearch snippets, a weaker verification path than usual. WebSearch quota was also exhausted mid-collection. A possible 'Closed-Loop Cooling Explained' infrastructure post on about.fb.com (URL path suggests August 2026) could not have its exact publication date confirmed as falling inside the 2026-08-29 to 2026-09-05 window, so it was excluded. A reported consumer AI agent platform ('Hatch') for Instagram/WhatsApp was covered in trade press this week but appears based on unnamed-source reporting rather than an official Meta announcement as of 2026-09-05, so it was excluded per sourcing rules. Meta's contribution of SAM 3 and DINOv3 to the US Department of Energy's Genesis Mission was found via an official ai.meta.com blog post, but that announcement dates to around July 22, 2026 — outside the 10-day freshness window and not newly relevant this week — so it was excluded. Given these constraints, only one item met confidence and recency requirements for this window.
